title: One UI 9 Exits Beta and Arrives on Galaxy S26
seoTitle: One UI 9 Exits Beta, Rolls Out to Galaxy S26 Series
subtitle: Samsung Launches New Android 17-Based Layer for S26 Series
excerpt: Samsung has concluded the One UI 9 beta period and released the official version for Galaxy S26, S26+, and S26 Ultra models, bringing features from the Galaxy Z Fold 8.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Samsung has concluded the One UI 9 beta period and, this Wednesday (16), began rolling out the official version for the Galaxy S26 line. The release brings features to the phone that were previously restricted to the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

What One UI 9 Based on Android 17 Brings

The new interface layer is built on Android 17, offering performance improvements and advanced feature integration. Among the features highlighted by the manufacturer are usability adjustments and new additions that enhance the user experience.

How the Distribution is Being Carried Out

The update is being delivered gradually. Samsung has not set specific dates for each region, but typically begins the rollout in South Korea, the company's home country, and then expands to Europe, North America, and Latin America, including Brazil.

Models Already Receiving the Update

Currently, One UI 9 is available only for the Galaxy S26, S26+, and S26 Ultra. Other devices from the brand will also enter the update cycle, according to the support period announced by the company.

Impact for Brazilian Users

For consumers in Brazil, the arrival of One UI 9 means immediate access to innovations that were previously exclusive to foldable devices. The stability achieved after the beta period should ensure a more fluid and secure experience.

Samsung's Next Steps

The company indicated that it will continue to expand One UI 9 support to other models in its lineup, adhering to the update schedule planned for each device. Interested users can follow the release on technology news platforms to find out when the package will arrive on their devices.

With information from Estadão.
